item.title: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.28581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Cramp\'e in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, together with four other decompositions of $V$ said to be split. We show that on each decomposition, every element of the first two bases acts in a block diagonal, block upper bidiagonal, block lower bidiagonal, or block tridiagonal fashion. We illustrate these actions using a tetrahedron diagram. We also determine how the elements of the third basis act on the six decompositions. To obtain our results about finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-modules, we use the theory of tridiagonal pairs.
item.dc:creator: Jae-Ho Lee

item.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties. As applications, we realize the irreducible polynomial representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n}$ on the relevant homology of the fibers of these maps, establish a geometric $(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n},\mathfrak{gl}_{k|l})$-Howe duality and confirm new cases of a conjecture of Douglass and R\"ohrle on generalized Steinberg varieties.
item.dc:creator: Yang Yang

item.title: An explicit BGG-type resolution of the spin/oscillator module for osp(2m+1|2n)
item.description: arXiv:2611.29264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit resolution of the spin/oscillator representation of the Lie superalgebra osp(2m+1|2n) by parabolic Verma modules. The resolution appears as the Chevalley-Eilenberg chain complex of the Lie algebra of quadratic operators in the universal Heisenberg algebra of the vector superspace C^{m|n}. In particular, its differentials are given by unified linear algebra formulas and all have degree 2 with respect to the standard grading of Verma modules.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Kapranov, Vera Serganova

item.title: Hilbert measures of non-coregular representations of the circle and orthogonal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give explicit constructions of the Hilbert measure, which transports the integral of an invariant smooth function from a representation to the image of the Hilbert embedding, for certain representations of the circle, orthogonal, and special orthogonal groups that are non-coregular, meaning that the algebra of invariants is not a polynomial algebra. These include all $4$-dimension real circle representations, a family of $6$-dimensional circle representations, and $k$ copies of the defining representations of the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups when $k$ is large enough that the representation is not coregular. For the circle representations, we also construct the Hilbert measure on the singular symplectic quotient at level zero.
item.dc:creator: Luca Liebow, Belle Roberge, Christopher Seaton

item.title: Resolution of ladder representations for classical groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atobe has introduced ladder representations of the $p$-adic groups $\mathbf{Sp}(2n)$ and $\mathbf{SO}(2n+1)$, which contain the strongly positive discrete series and M\oe glin's representations attached to irreducible Arthur parameters, and has expressed their characters as alternating sums of costandard modules. We show that all the coefficients of this formula are $\pm1$, with the sign given by the dimension of the orbit of the Langlands parameter, and that these representations have coresolutions of Cousin type by costandard modules, whose Euler characteristic is Atobe's formula.
item.dc:creator: David. A. Renard

item.title: Metric structure in Hecke-induced modules for groups acting on buildings
item.description: arXiv:2611.30901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a thick locally finite building of type $(W, S)$ and $G$ be a locally compact group acting properly and chamber-transitively on $X$. We give a condition on a Hermitian module $(V_0, \varphi_0)$ of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $\mathbf C_{\mathbf q}[W]$ ensuring that the natural $G$-invariant form defined on the induced $G$-module has the same negative index as $\varphi_0$, where ${\mathbf q}$ is the thickness vector of $X$. It implies that induction of Hecke-modules preserves unitarity. In the affine case, this recovers results by Matsumoto, Barbasch--Moy and Ciubotaru. In general, assuming that $G$ is Weyl-transitive, we obtain new irreducible $G$-representations on Hilbert spaces as well as on infinite-dimensional symmetric spaces of finite rank. Using Hecke-modules of Lorentzian signature, we also derive new obstructions to Kazhdan's property (T), showing that the known sufficient conditions in terms of the thickness are mostly necessary.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Emmanuel Caprace, Alex Lou\'e, Andreas Thom

item.title: The index from a super-point
item.description: arXiv:2611.28204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, the ideal is the sum of the Jacobian ideals of a single superpotential and of its two supersymmetry variations. For $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, the ideal is similarly the sum of the Jacobian ideals of the components of a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ superfield, which is a singlet of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ flavor symmetry for gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and a triplet for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The associated VOA for the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ theory is given by the Feigin--Feigin--Tipunin $\mathcal{A}(6)$ algebra. The arc space of Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of $\mathcal{A}(6)$ does not reproduce the vacuum character, and therefore $\mathcal{A}(6)$ is not classically free. Supplementing Zhu's $C_2$-algebra by three relations in the first jet ring, the generalized arc space reproduces the Macdonald index of $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ up to, at least, order $q^{51}$.
item.dc:creator: Dhanvarsh Annamalai, Hyunook Hur, Thomas Hussel, Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song

item.title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schr\"odinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Sch\"orkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix structure prohibits a straightforward supersymmetric removal. To circumvent this, we transform the equation to a Schr\"odinger operator with drift terms to simplify the structure of the eigenfunction. We then develop tools to study such operators and conclude that said operator has no second negative eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: Josef E. Greilhuber, David Wallauch

item.title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-module. Its lowest generalized $L(0)$-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and $L(0)$ acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue $-2$.
item.dc:creator: Dra\v{z}en Adamovi\'c, Ivana Vukorepa

item.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.
item.dc:creator: Egor Ryzhkin, Vladimir Stukopin

item.title: Uniform dominance of Golod local rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.28910v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every Golod local ring $R$ is uniformly dominant. More precisely, we show that its dominant index is at most the embedding dimension of $R$. The proof is based on a numerical criterion for formality of bounded complexes whose homology is annihilated by the maximal ideal.
item.dc:creator: Toshinori Kobayashi, Yuki Mifune

item.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.29063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the left ideal ${\rm cl}(L)$ under the classification of ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ given in [Berest--Chalykh, 2012]. The proof is based on a dual version of the Cannings--Holland correspondence, which describes left ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ in terms of finite-dimensional spaces of algebraic distributions on $X$, and an explicit formula for the Calogero--Moser index given in terms of these distributions. We apply these results to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions on $X$: we call a holonomic function $f$ strongly holonomic if the Calogero--Moser index of ${\rm Ann}_{\mathcal D}(f)$ is positive, and we compute this index in a number of interesting cases.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Berest, Isaac Goldberg

item.title: Blocks with one simple module and solvable groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $b$ be a block of a finite group with one isomorphism class of simple modules in characteristic $p$. We construct, over a sufficiently large complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, a Morita equivalence between $b$ and a block of a finite solvable group. The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.
item.dc:creator: Kun Zhang, Yuanyang Zhou

item.title: The Geometry of Banach space operator-valued measures with cyclic dilations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the geometric properties of operator-valued measures with cyclic dilations. Under a localization condition on the normal part of the bidual, we establish James-type characterizations of shrinking, bounded completeness, and reflexivity for projection-valued measures. These characterizations apply to spaces admitting no continuous Schauder frame, including $L_1[0,1]$. Using vector measure representations and interpolation, we prove that an operator-valued measure admitting a cyclic dilation has a reflexive cyclic dilation if and only if the underlying space is reflexive. Under the same cyclicity assumption, we also characterize the existence of cyclic dilations on spaces containing no $\ell_1$ and on KB-spaces. The dilation spaces can be chosen to be order-continuous K\"othe function spaces. Without assuming cyclicity, we give a weak compactness criterion and local variation conditions for reflexive dilations; an example on $\ell_2$ shows that reflexivity alone is insufficient. For a separable space containing no $c_0$, a normalized operator-valued measure is induced by a continuous Schauder frame if and only if it admits a cyclic dilation and has $\sigma$-finite operator-norm variation. Finally, for measure quotients whose synthesis maps admit bounded linear right inverses, we construct compatible cyclic $L_p$-dilations and represent the quotient spaces as inductive limits, with applications to ReLU Barron spaces.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Freeman, Qianfeng Hu, Rui Liu, Jie Shen

item.title: Principal subspaces of affine vertex algebras at admissible levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.29412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify generic principal subspaces of admissible affine vertex algebras for all simple Lie algebras. The nongeneric cases occur precisely at denominator two in types $B,C,F_4$ and at denominator three in type $G_2$. The proof uses geometry of nilpotent orbits combined with positive root null vectors. Surprisingly, null vectors needed for our classification are explicitly known and already studied in the literature. We then study the exceptional principal subspaces at the level of their $C_2$-algebras and arc algebras. For $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ at level $-\frac12$ and $G_2$ at level $-\frac53$, we prove classical freeness and obtain product character formulas. In type $C_n$ at level $-\frac12$, classical freeness fails for $n\ge4$. For $n=3$, we combine the functional model method of Feigin and Stoyanovsky, and a flat degeneration of the explicit realization of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ to prove a product character formula, while classical freeness in this case remains conjectural. The principal subspace of $L_{-5/2}(F_4)$ is also conjecturally classically free.
item.dc:creator: Hao Li, Antun Milas

item.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.
item.dc:creator: Satoshi Naito, Khanh Nguyen Duc, Daisuke Sagaki

item.title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2611.29667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.
item.dc:creator: John W. MacQuarrie, Peter Symonds

item.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.29713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Ahsan Z. Khan

item.title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
item.description: arXiv:2611.29860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.
item.dc:creator: Pavlo Pylyavskyy

item.title: Orbital Integrals on Unitary Groups and Zeta Values
item.description: arXiv:2611.29994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize Yun's interpolation formula for orbital integrals on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in terms of Dedekind zeta functions to stable orbital integrals on unitary groups. Our approach combines Xiao's germ expansion of orbital integrals and the Jacquet-Rallis fundamental lemma.
item.dc:creator: Li Cai, Xuan Cui

item.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
item.description: arXiv:2207.03115v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Braverman, Michael Finkelberg, Roman Travkin

item.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
item.description: arXiv:2404.18939v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by F\'elix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Zhou

item.title: Arthur packets for metaplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2410.13606v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For metaplectic groups over a local field of characteristic zero, we define the Arthur packet attached to any Arthur parameter $\psi$ as a multi-set of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterized by endoscopic character relations. Over number fields, we obtain a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete $L^2$-automorphic spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and $\epsilon$-factors, by leveraging the trace formula for metaplectic groups. This confirms a conjecture of Gan, and extends earlier results of Gan-Ichino on the Shimura-Waldspurger correspondences, whereas their works play a critical role in our proof. Furthermore, all these are shown to be compatible with existing results in rank one (Waldspurger) and two (Gan-Ichino).
item.dc:creator: Wen-Wei Li

item.title: Exact Solutions to the Klein--Gordon Equation via Reduction Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2507.04572v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reduction algebras (also known as generalized Mickelsson algebras, Zhelobenko algebras, or transvector algebras) are well-studied associative algebras appearing in the representation theory of Lie algebras. In the 1990s, Zhelobenko noted that reduction algebras have a connection to field equations from physics, whereas Howe's study of dual pairs in the 1980s signifies that the link originated even earlier. In this paper, we revisit the simplest case of a massless scalar field, in arbitrary spacetime dimension $n\ge 3$ and arbitrary flat metric $\eta_{ab}$; the field equation then specializes to the Laplace equation and to the massless Klein--Gordon equation. The relevant reduction algebra comes from a representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (technically, $\mathfrak{sp}_2$) by differential operators. We give a complete presentation of this reduction algebra. Its raising operators produce bosonic states $|a_1a_2\cdots a_\ell\rangle$, polynomial solutions of degree $\ell$ to the field equation, and we show that the natural bilinear form on these states is computed by symmetrizers built from the rational dynamical R-matrix. Along the way we give explicit formulas for the states, and a self-contained proof, for a general metric, of Zhelobenko's results that they span the polynomial solutions and that the solution space is an irreducible module over the reduction algebra.
item.dc:creator: Jonas T. Hartwig, Lillian Ryan Uhl, Dwight Anderson Williams II

item.title: The Balmer spectrum of integral permutation modules
item.description: arXiv:2507.05892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules of a finite group over a commutative Noetherian ring. In this generality, we obtain a set-theoretic description of the spectrum. Under certain mild additional assumptions on the base ring, we describe its topology by reducing the problem first to the modular locus and then to the case of elementary abelian groups. Furthermore, we introduce a twisted cohomology ring in this context, which allows us to realize the spectrum, in the case of elementary abelian $p$-groups, as a Dirac scheme. This extends recent work of Balmer and Gallauer from the setting of ground fields to the more general setting of commutative Noetherian rings.
item.dc:creator: Umesh V Dubey, Juan Omar G\'omez

item.title: Dirac reduction algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.21730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: There is a homomorphism of associative superalgebras from the enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to the Weyl-Clifford superalgebra $A(2n|n)$ with $2n$ even Weyl algebra generators and $n$ odd Clifford algebra generators. Under this homomorphism, the positive odd root vector $x\in\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is sent to the Dirac operator $\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\in A(2n|n)$ and generates a left ideal $I$. The corresponding reduction (super)algebra, denoted $Z_n$, is the normalizer of $I$ in $A(2n|n)$ modulo $I$. By construction, $Z_n$ acts on the space of all Clifford algebra-valued polynomial solutions to the (massless) Dirac equation. This setting goes back to Zhelobenko, who described generators of this reduction algebra and commutation relations among them. In this paper, we find a complete presentation of (a localization of) this so-termed Dirac reduction algebra, with full proofs. We give a closed formula for products of the raising operators in the reduction algebra and use it to write down explicitly the polynomial solutions to the Dirac equation in $n$-dimensional flat spacetime that they generate. Finally, we show that for $n\neq 2$ the space of polynomial solutions is irreducible over the reduction algebra tensored with the opposite Clifford algebra when $n$ is even, and is a direct sum of two irreducible submodules when $n$ is odd.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Dorang, Jonas T. Hartwig, Dwight Anderson Williams II

item.title: Koszulity in the category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie Superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$
item.description: arXiv:2604.10388v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main result of this paper is to establish precisely which blocks in the Category $\mathcal{O}$ of the periplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{pe}(2)$ are Koszul. It is known that $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ has three blocks up to equivalence; one generic block and two integral blocks. The generic block is known to be Koszul, and the principle integral block is verifiably not Koszul. In this paper, we prove that the remaining of the three blocks of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul. Consequently every non-principal block of $\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{pe}(2))$ is Koszul, which is the category $\mathcal{O}$ analogue, in the smallest case, of a known result for finite-dimensional modules over semisimple extensions of Takiff superalgebras. This is done by explicitly computing the endomorphism algebra of projective modules in this block and then proving that it is Koszul inductively. Along the way, we compute all $\mathrm{Ext}$ groups between simples in this block. To compute the endomorphism algebra we are aided by a computer algebra tool developed in Mathematica, inspired by a post on Stack Exchange.
item.dc:creator: Finn Kinley

item.title: Gelfand--Kirillov dimensions of highest weight modules for basic classical Lie superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.11551v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain explicit formulas for the Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimensions of simple highest weight modules over basic classical Lie superalgebras. For the type II orthosymplectic superalgebras $D(m,n)$ and $B(m,n)$, we describe the associated varieties determined by highest weights relative to two Borel subalgebras. This gives algorithms valid for arbitrary complex highest weights, without integrality or typicality hypotheses. In type $B$, we further derive a formula for $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$, distinguishing between integral and half-integral weights. For $G(3)$, $F(4)$ and $D(2,1;\alpha)$, finite odd-reflection procedures give exact GK dimension formulas and finite-dimensionality criteria. We also describe the dependence on $\alpha$ for $D(2,1;\alpha)$. In type I, the GK dimension equals that of the simple even highest weight module for the distinguished Borel subalgebra. The computations rely on established ordinary Lie algebra formulas involving Lusztig's $\mathbf a$-function and Robinson--Schensted (RS) insertion.
item.dc:creator: Jing Jiang

item.title: Nilpotent quiver varieties with multiplicities and symmetrisable crystals
item.description: arXiv:2607.17301v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct analogues of Nakajima's nilpotent quiver varieties for quivers with multiplicities, by developing new stability conditions for framed nilpotent quiver representations with multiplicities and exploiting their interplay with Hecke correspondences. Using these new quiver varieties, we extend Saito's geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals of irreducible highest-weight representations of Kac--Moody algebras from the symmetric to the symmetrisable case.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Hoskins, Joshua Jackson, Tanguy Vernet

item.title: Orbits of submaximal dimension for Sylow $p$-subgroups of finite classical orthogonal groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.27525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $U$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup in a classical orthogonal group over a finite field with $q$ elements of characteristic $p$ large enough. The coadjoint orbits of the group $U$ play the key role in the description of irreducible complex characters of $U$. In the paper, we provide a classification of such orbits of pre-maximal dimension. As a corollary, we compute the number of all orbits mentioned above. It turned out that each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q - 1$ with integer non-negative coefficients, which agrees with the Isaacs' conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Ignatev, Mikhail Venchakov

item.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.30740v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2609.25045v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schr\"{o}dinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Takahashi

item.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.22156v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. These are double affine versions of the quantum affine wreath algebras of Rosso and Savage. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite cyclic group, we obtain new double affine versions of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the supercentre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Niccol\`o Mattarei

item.title: Some results on representation type and Galois covering with application to the associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove some general results on representation types of special biserial algebras and on Galois coverings of quivers with relations. Moreover, combining these results with the covering theory of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras we determine the representation types of the associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras.
item.dc:creator: Jing Guo, Nengqun Li, Yuming Liu

item.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.29750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_{\chi})$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.
item.dc:creator: Yumeng Wu, Jie Xiao

item.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32040v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.
item.dc:creator: Kyu-Hwan Lee, Euiyong Park

item.title: On the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.16017v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Eteve

item.title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
item.description: arXiv:2611.18938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.
item.dc:creator: G. Lusztig

item.title: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.21912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Brou\'e, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Brou\'e, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.
item.dc:creator: Eirini Chavli, Maria Chlouveraki, G\"otz Pfeiffer, Kostas Psaromiligkos

item.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2409.16571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].
item.dc:creator: Danielle Ernst-West, Doron Puder, Yotam Shomroni

item.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
item.description: arXiv:2505.09996v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.
item.dc:creator: Priya Dhankhar, Sanjay Kumar Singh

item.title: Tensor ideals of abelian type and quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.08859v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate a study of tensor ideals in linear rigid monoidal categories that are kernels of linear monoidal functors to abelian monoidal categories. We develop general methods and apply them to the category of tilting modules over quantum groups as well as to some representation categories of finite groups. In an appendix on Duflo involutions in monoidal categories, we make a connection between Duflo involutions in the affine Weyl group and tensor ideals for quantum groups, and prove some of Lusztig's conjectures for arbitrary Coxeter groups, at equal parameters, without invoking the boundedness hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier, Pavel Etingof, Victor Ostrik

item.title: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.09471v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.
item.dc:creator: Hicham Assakaf

item.title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.23240v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic \'etale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehat{\Xi}_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehat{\Xi}_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite \'etale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $\mu_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.
item.dc:creator: David Kazhdan

item.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14507v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. In the Szeg\H{o} setting, local rigidity was established by Lu--Tian (2004) on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and, more recently, by Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026) on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqin Lu, Yuang Shi

item.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.24594v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $\lambda$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+\lambda=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.24802v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.
item.dc:creator: Jelena Ivan\v{c}i\'c
